utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see anything in the office, apart from the people who beat me, who interrogated me, and I saw a picture of Khomeini on the wall. That's what I noticed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many times did you -- were you taken into that office?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: I was taken to the office on five days. They would sometimes cover my head with a jacket. When they took me to the office, and then they would take me from the office up to the room. I didn't see movement around me. That's where I would relieve myself and do everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you were in the process of describing the people that you saw in the office when my friend interjected. Could you describe the people that you saw in the office.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They all had beards. I didn't know them, but the person who interrogated me also had a beard, but he spoke my own language, so I could understand him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you form any opinion as to the nationality or the origin of the persons you saw in the room where you were being interrogated?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They would all say "Selaam". They were all Muslims. But as to why they came from, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that they had beards, is there anything else that you saw about them?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They had BH army inscriptions on them that said "the 7th Muslim Brigade." This is what they had on their arms. And they had green headbands on too, with an inscription in Arabic. This is something I couldn't understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, apart from the person that you saw in the room when you had occasion to go there, were there guards at the Music School that you saw?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They didn't allow me to see anything. All I did was go up and down the stairs. I never went outside. When they took me to the prison, they did so at night. I didn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They took you to which prison at night, are you speaking of?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: To the Zenica KP Dom, the penal and correctional facility, on the 2nd of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who took you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Two of these bearded men. They only handed me over at the gate. The person on duty took charge of me. I have a record of this. They didn't give me a paper of any kind. But these people registered me and took me to a cell. Later they brought another four Croats there who told me that they were from Catici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's return to the Music School. Can you say which unit the persons that you saw in the room when you were being interrogated belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They were all members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the witness has answered this question already. He already answered the question when the Prosecution asked him about this. He said that he could clearly recognise the markings of the unit concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stamp. He has already answered this question. You asked him this question. He said it was the 7th Brigade. So asking the same question again is not useful. He's answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I will abide by your ruling. But may I just say, Mr. President, with respect, that earlier he said that he observed their insignias -- the insignias being that of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Now he's saying that they were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade. That is not forensically speaking, precisely the same thing. There might be other reasons why he might be able to tell the Court why they were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, I will just move on to ask this question. Why do you say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if you want him to answer more precisely, you can ask the witness your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say they were members of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: I knew them from Kakanj and I recognised them to be members of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you elaborate a little bit further on your answer?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: When I went to see Mustafa, the secretary, he also told me that Halid Cengic sent him that unit. They took him on as a lawyer and he remained there to work for them. He asked me whether I would join. I told him that I was employed. I worked in the field of security in my company, in the Catici power plant. I didn't accept the offer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the secretary of the 7th Muslim Brigade tell you anything about these bearded men?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: He told me that these were good men, that they were working in the name of Allah, in order to defend the Muslims, and that mostly volunteers from Islamic world had come. But some local men had also joined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell -- did he tell you about his role, as secretary of the 7th Muslim Brigade, in respect to these volunteers?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: He just said that he was a reliable official --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the witness has already expressed his opinion about the role of the secretary during his testimony, that he kept records and a registry of members. I think he gave a clear answer to this question already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Stamp. As you asked him already about the person he knew, that is, the secretary of the 7th Brigade, who was a lawyer, he told us what he did. But if you are asking this question, I assume you have a purpose. But in the way in which the question has been worded, then it is quite right to say that it has already been asked and answered. Please continue, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did he tell you about his role as secretary of the 7th Muslim Brigade in respect to these volunteers that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: That he was working on their registration, as a lawyer, because he's qualified to do that, and that Halid Cengic had appointed him to this position, Halid Cengic being from Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just tell us, in a sentence, what was the office of Halid Cengic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Halid Cengic was the chief of logistics for the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, allegedly, at the time, and he was based in Visoko, and he fled Foca and came there and abandoned Foca. And I inquired what he was doing there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Nothing further.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That is the examination-in-chief, may it please you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is noon. I think it would be better to have our 25-minute break now, and we will resume at 25 past 12.00. The Chamber may have a couple of questions for the witness, perhaps, and then I will give the floor to the Defence for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Before giving the floor to Defence counsel for the cross-examination, the Chamber would like to address the witness for two points of clarification. One has the impression, listening to you, that when you were at the Sretno Motel, apart from the people that were going to interrogate you, as you said, you didn't see anyone else, and the Chamber would like to know whether, at the Sretno Motel, you saw other detainees. Were there other detainees there or were you the only detainee held in a room there? Were there other people there? What can you tell us about that? Because you spent several days there. Yes, Mr. Stamp. I'm not asking you the question. It is the witness I'm addressing myself to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. With respect, I understood that. I just want to raise a point of clarification. I think the witness did not indicate that he was detained at the Sretno Motel, but that he was detained at the Zenica Music School. Just a matter of clarification, if I may be of assistance to the Court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, Mr. Stamp. When you were at the Sretno Motel, were there other people in addition to you, or were you alone there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was alone, seeing the secretary, Mustafa Oprasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how long did you stay there at the Sretno Motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For as long as it took for us to have a cup of coffee, 10 or 15 minutes, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And then afterwards, when you were at the KP Dom, you spent several days there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 101.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And at the KP Dom, you saw other detainees, or were you alone in your cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first night I spent with four Croats who also came beaten up, covered in blood, and one of them was with me for 101 days, Tomic Marin in cell number 1, and he stayed behind when I left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And do you know why you were in such a position at all? You had a job. Why did you find yourself in that position for 101 days? Were you given an explanation subsequently or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was, because I sued -- I started proceedings in the state court in Sarajevo, and I was told that Halid Cengic ordered my arrest. I know everything. I wrote everything down as to who betrayed Foca, and that is the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Podrug. My name is Edina Residovic and I'm Defence counsel for General Enver Hadzihasanovic. In answer to a question by my learned friend, or rather, strike that. Is it true, Mr. Podrug, that, as of 1963, you started working in the State Security Service of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No, not state security, but the security of the building site of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Hidrogradnja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the very beginning, you joined in the defence of the country and the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Foca?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, correct. I have all the ID cards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Foca fell into the hands of the Serb forces, you went to Hrasnica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There you worked in your company, Hidrogradnja, under work obligation rules; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is there that you were wounded and then transferred to Fojnica; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you told my learned friend, your manager appointed you to provide security for the thermal power plant in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: There was the mechanical equipment within the compound that I needed to watch over and secure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You visited the Sretno Motel simply to see your friend from Foca, Mustafa Oprasic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't inquire into the structure of the army and the police, but you just learned some things along the way; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, because I was a member of the Executive Council on behalf of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Music School that you described for my learned friend, you spent seven days in that school and you had no document about your arrest?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No, I had nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the KP Dom, criminal proceedings were instituted against you for a serious crime of which you were later acquitted?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes. I was accused of serving the enemy army, the HVO in Kiseljak, which is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned -- strike that. Actually, you believe that Halid Cengic was responsible for what happened to you, and he's also from Foca?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, correct, and he was a deputy, just like I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a member of the army from the beginning, the proceedings against you, even though you were acquitted, hurt you badly, and you are very bitter about everything that happened to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, and I immediately left the SDA party when I was released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You believe that this person was the logistics chief for the whole Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that he was a powerful man, and that he was able to do that to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: He was the most powerful man, even more powerful than Alija Izetbegovic, he and his son Hasan Cengic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Podrug, that because of this bitterness that you harbour for being accused of such a grave crime while being a fighter, you spoke repeatedly about this?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes. I spoke for three hours for the media, and asked Alija Izetbegovic to join me for the people to hear what we had to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Podrug.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give the floor now to the other Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. On behalf of Mr. Kubura's Defence, we too have a few questions for today's witness. Cross-examined by Mr. Ibrisimovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Podrug, in the course of the examination-in-chief today, in answer to a question from my learned friend, you said that on the 27th of July you were in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, you were really living in Kakanj, where you were under work obligation?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No, I was not living in Kakanj. I had no accommodation. I worked there and I used the power plant's bus to travel daily from Visoko to Catici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, members of the 7th Muslim Brigade who introduced themselves came to fetch you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, that is true. I have witness, Hadzan Kubat, that I stayed with in his house in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they told you that they were taking you to the brigade headquarters to talk to the commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You thought you were going to the Sretno Motel, where, in your opinion, the brigade headquarters was situated?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, because I had seen Brzina two days prior to that, visiting Halid Cengic in Visoko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The brigade command of the 7th Muslim Brigade was in the Sretno Motel in Kakanj, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that, you mentioned that you had been to the Sretno Motel on a couple of occasions to talk to the brigade secretary, Mr. Oprasic?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Only once. I learned that he was there, and I wanted to inquire what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your conversation lasted ten minutes or so?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, for as long as it took us to have a cup of coffee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he himself tell you that he was the secretary of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: He told me that, because he was a lawyer by profession, and I know that he was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that a brigade, a military unit, according to establishment, cannot have a secretary?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: It can have a lawyer, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Osman Hasanagic? Does the name mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, according to your testimony, you were familiar with the command personnel of the 7th Muslim Brigade. You said that the commander of that brigade was Brzina.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: I saw him with Halid Cengic in Visoko two days prior to this, and his driver told me that it was Halil Brzina, the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you personally knew that he was commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No. [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you got into the car, which you described as a Lada vehicle, and when you passed through Kakanj, you went on to Zenica and you said to a building that you didn't know.

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know where the Music School was, nor was I ever interested in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, you learnt that it was the Music School building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that, you'd never been to the Music School in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your testimony today and the examination-in-chief, you said that you were interrogated on a number of occasions in the Music School

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and beaten up. I am -- I have a disability pension because of the beating. I bled for a whole month, and Marin Tomic is a witness of that. I left the prison and I weighed only 48 kilogrammes when I left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding the persons interrogating you, you were unable to recognise them, nor did you know where they were from?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No. I didn't know any of them. They were just bearded, wearing uniforms. I saw their insignia, and they had headbands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't speak to any one of them, except the person who was interrogating you?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: No one wanted to talk. I assume they were foreigners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spent only seven days in the Music School?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, and they took me to the KP Dom at night. The Croats were brought to this cell. We were sitting there all together in a single cell, and all of us were covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the Music School, you learnt why you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: They told me I was an enemy of my own people, and I said I was a personal friend of Alija Izetbegovic and his bodyguard, and I have IDs to prove it, and everyone knows that. I was a counsel on behalf of the SDA. I enjoyed immunity. But they had no regard for that. They beat me. They said: What do you mean, Alija? Who have you been writing to? Et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In answer to a question from the President, you said that you started proceedings in the court in Sarajevo on account of this. And these proceedings were designed to achieve compensation for damages?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The proceedings ended, and it was rejected?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, because the case was returned to Zenica and then it became outdated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like the witness to be shown a document compiled by his solicitor from Sarajevo regarding the proceedings for compensation of damages. The source of the document is the Prosecution. We received the document from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think the witness has been given the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a complaint made by your lawyers, Hadziahmetovic, Hidajet, a lawyer from Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Defence, please. Could Defence counsel please repeat the question, as the microphone was not switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of the first and second page, I think we can see your signature. You can have a look at it. It's to the right. Was Hidajet Hadziahmetovic your lawyer, a lawyer from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he represent you in this lawsuit?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a lawsuit that he filed on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes, but there is just one mistake here. I wasn't a member of the army. I was performing my work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your lawyer probably compiled this following your instructions. In this lawsuit, you said that you were asking for compensation for having been illegally detained in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes. From the 2nd of August, they tried to shorten this for a month, but this was finally detected. One knows when I was taken to prison, when I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since the witness has recognised this lawsuit compiled by his lawyer, Hidajet Hadziahmetovic, from Sarajevo, we suggest that this lawsuit be accepted -- be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm addressing the Defence. Because we have a text, a document in B/C/S, and we have two English translations, one which must correspond to the trial judgement and the second English text concerns the appeal proceedings, apparently. Apparently there was a judgement from the Sarajevo court on the 28th of December, 1999. And the appeals Chamber. That was on the 3rd of May, 2000. The B/C/S text corresponds to what, exactly? Apparently, this should be the judgement rendered by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we only suggested that the lawsuit be shown to the witness, since he has already said that it was rejected by the relevant court in Sarajevo. That's why we didn't suggest that it be tendered into evidence. It's probably a mistake. The fact that you have both documents is probably a mistake. We're only talking about the lawsuit and the request to institute proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. What I was saying is that the English text, or English texts' translation, if I'm not mistaken, I have the impression that the English text that has to do with the appeal proceedings is a text that we don't have in the B/C/S version. As you have the documents before you, you could check this. I only have one document in B/C/S, and I have two English translations. One is a judgement rendered by the municipal court in Sarajevo, and the second one has been issued by the appeals chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'll withdraw the document, that is, the judgement. We only want to tender into evidence the document that concerns instituting proceedings. We have provided a translation of this document in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. What does the Prosecution have to say about having this document, these documents tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: What my friend is trying to do is to tender the lawsuit and its translation. There was an error in adding the translation in respect of the appeal. Normally I would not really object to a request of this nature, but it appears to me to be outside of the precise terms of the ruling of the Court in respect to what the witness could be asked about. The precise terms of the ruling [Microphone not activated] Asked about appears on page 36, from line 14 [Microphone not activated]. What is being asked now is clearly outside of those precise terms. Apart from that, I have no objection to this course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in response to a question that you put to the witness, the witness spoke about the lawsuit and the proceedings that were instituted in Sarajevo. This document is one we have suggested, as we want to check this witness's credibility. But as our learned colleague has no objection to raise, we stand by our request to have this document tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll mark this document for identification, and the Trial Chamber will deliberate on what to do with this document at a later date. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for this document, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the B/C/S document will get Exhibit number DK 9, and it's English translation of the claim gets the Exhibit number DK9/E.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has been marked for identification, Mr. Registrar. We will deliberate about the document after the hearing. Please continue, if you have any further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is there any re-examination for the Prosecution? Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is something that arose out of questions that were put to the witness by the Trial Chamber, and that is in respect of the Motel Sretno and the series of events. I merely want to ask him whether or not his coffee with the person that he described to be the secretary of the 7th Muslim Brigade occurred before or after his detention at the Zenica Music School. Re-examined by Mr. Stamp:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you understand that question, Mr. Podrug? When you spoke with --

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: Yes. I had a coffee before I was detained and before I met Halid Cengic, and that is where I saw Halil Brzina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall exactly which unit had its headquarters at the Hotel Sretno?

utterances.speaker: ALIJA PODRUG
utterances.text: There was only the unit of the 7th Muslim Brigade. That's what Mr. Mustafa Oprasic told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, although the witness has already answered this question again, this is a question that the witness answered in the course of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's already on the record, but not precisely the same thing. Slightly different scope, it is submitted. That will be all, may it please Mr. President. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Podrug, you have come to testify here at the request of the Prosecution. You were only to testify about the facts that you witnessed, because, unfortunately, your personal situation is not one included in the allegations made in the indictment. And this is why what happened to you personally was not a matter that could be discussed, given that the allegations that concern your personal situation are not allegations with which the accused can be charged. You yourself told us spontaneously, without having been asked about this, that certain things had happened to you. You also mentioned that you had instituted proceedings in courts. As a result, your personal situation must have been dealt with before the national courts. This is not a matter that we can deal with. So we just wanted to inform you that you were not in a position to testify about what happened to you personally, but only about what you saw. You have answered the questions put to you by the Prosecution, as well as the questions put to you by the Defence. You have also answered the Trial Chamber's questions. We are grateful for your answers. We wish you a good trip home. And I'm now going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just rise to indicate, Mr. President, Your Honour, that as a matter of fairness, the objection to the document presented by my friend is withdrawn. Clearly, it's relevant and something the Court should consider. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will deliberate on the matter. We have a little more time. There are no more witnesses scheduled for today. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's no further witness scheduled for today. In respect to the witness who's scheduled tomorrow, can I please ask to go into private session to raise an issue related to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. At this point in time, the Defence would like to inform the Trial Chamber that we have taken certain steps. About a month ago we took certain steps. The Trial Chamber was informed of this through the legal officer, and the Prosecution was also informed of this, as well as the Registry. We would like to inform the Trial Chamber that we have obtained a model that represents Central Bosnia. This model arrived yesterday evening. Mr. President, we would like to be able to use this model in the course of examination-in-chief and the cross-examination of certain witnesses. Nevertheless, there are a number of difficulties. This model is fairly large. It consists of six parts. And in our opinion -- we haven't put all the parts together yet, but in our opinion, the size of the model would be three metres by two metres. We'll check this, and this should enable us to place the model in the middle of the courtroom. We have discussed this possibility with the Prosecution. The Prosecution has told us that they have no objections to us using the model. Our intention would be to have the model in the courtroom for one witness who could identify it, and then we would only use parts of the model for certain witnesses. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you prepare an order so that we can have the reference to this witness redacted from the transcript. It's page 67, line 12. The interpreters' booth has said that the Prosecution also made reference to the name. If that is the case, the name should be redacted in this case too. Mr. Registrar, you'll prepare the order for me. You may continue, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. At this point in time, the hearing of this witness should commence in Courtroom II on Thursday. This will not make it possible for us to use the model in question. And on Friday morning, I think that we will be back in Courtroom III. And that is when we would be able to use the model. We will immediately establish contact with the Registry and the security services after this hearing, to organise everything to have the model installed before the hearing on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a technical matter. Given that you want to use this model when cross-examining a witness, will you be requesting that the model be admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it is not our intention to request that the model be admitted into evidence. What we want to do is to have a witness identify the model, the witness who will be heard on Thursday and Friday, in particular, and we would like it to be marked for identification. But we will not be requesting that it be tendered into evidence, unless the Trial Chamber thinks that this might be appropriate in the circumstances. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, with regard to the model, is there anything the Prosecution would like to say? Are there any objections you would like to raise? As far as I can remember, models have already been used in other cases. This would not be anything new. And it might be very useful. What is the Prosecution's position?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this is certainly completely correct. And as my learned colleague already indicated, on principle, the Prosecution has no objections in using such a model in the course of the court proceedings. However, the Prosecution would like to ask the learned colleagues to inform the Trial Chamber when, where, by whom, was this model created, and whether it shows anything in addition to the geographic features, geographical features in Central Bosnia. We will certainly reserve our final comments until the time the learned colleagues from the Defence side have provided some more information on the model to both the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think Mr. Bourgon will be able to respond to the extent that the main concern of the Prosecution is that if it merely reproduces the topography of the area, they have no objection. But if the model contains other elements that could cause problems, you -- can you tell us already at this point whether this model is simply a miniature model in six square metres of the region of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. What we can tell you at this stage is that this model is part of a much larger model which represents Bosnia as a whole. We have already had occasion to have a look at the model, but it arrived yesterday evening. It is still packed. And this afternoon, we are going to put it together, to make sure that it only represents the topography and nothing more than that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Be that as it may, the model can only be installed in Courtroom I or Courtroom III, because it's impossible to do it in Courtroom II. Are there any other questions? There don't appear to be any. We will meet again at 2.15 on Thursday, as tomorrow's hearing has been cancelled. So I invite everyone to come back to the courtroom planned for this trial on Thursday afternoon. The hearing is adjourned.
